How does this work?

The turtle reads each number in your chosen base, calculates a value from its digits, and uses the remainder to choose an action in the Rules tab.

For example, 3 in base 2 is 11. Its digit sum is 2, giving remainder 0 when divided by 2.

A finite pattern is not proof of a fractal. Try longer sequences to explore its structure.

Turn digits into movement

Left means counterclockwise. A turn alone does not move the turtle.

Every traveled edge becomes forbidden in both directions. Use unit steps and turns in multiples of 60°.

Initial marked edges 0

Orange edges are forbidden before the first instruction. Editing restarts the walk.

Click near an edge to toggle it. Drag to pan. The editor opens near the origin.

Reproducible random marks

Enclose marks every edge crossing the hexagon boundary, keeping the turtle inside.

Setups save the exact edge list. Maximum 512 initial edges.

A weight for every digit

Add these weights instead of the digit values. Negative whole numbers are allowed.

Negative sums wrap into remainders 0 through divisor − 1. Hidden weights are kept when the base changes.
